own_solution.law: C = eps0 A/(d - t + t/k) for a dielectric slab in a parallel-plate capacitor; Q = C V at fixed battery emf; dQ = (C' - C0) V
assumptions: battery stays connected so V = 12 V throughout
slab position between plates irrelevant (series layers)

defect_reasons.other: T9341 ('Before the slab was inserted, a 7.5 V cell ... was connected') does not say explicitly whether the cell remains in the circuit during insertion; I read it as remaining (total emf 19.5 V), but a reader could take it as removed before insertion, giving 720 pC.

notes: C' = 100 pF x 6/(3 + 3/4) = 160 pF, so dC = 60 pF; dQ = 60 pF x 12 V = 720 pC; with an added 7.5 V cell in series aiding, emf 19.5 V gives 60 x 19.5 = 1170 pC. T27DA and T0DBA give no voltage ('a small cell') while their apparent counterparts T8799 and T970C state 7.5 V; if these are meant as minimal-pair variants they differ in the number, though the difference cannot change a D answer. Sentences T6AD3 and T9341 also slightly strain the problem text, which names a 12 V battery as the source; with the cell added the capacitor is charged to 19.5 V, not 12 V, but this is not strictly a contradiction.
